subject: biology
title: Hormones in human reproduction and the menstrual cycle
key_idea: At puberty, oestrogen and testosterone cause the secondary sex characteristics to develop. In the menstrual cycle, FSH matures an egg, LH releases it, and oestrogen and progesterone build and maintain the lining of the uterus.

blocks.text: During puberty, reproductive hormones cause the secondary sex characteristics to develop. The main hormone differs in females and males.

items.meaning: A chemical messenger made in a gland and carried in the blood to a target organ.
The body changes at puberty, such as breast development in females.
The release of an egg from an ovary.

items: **Oestrogen** is the main female reproductive hormone. It is made in the ovary.
At puberty eggs begin to mature, and one is released about every 28 days. This is ovulation.
**Testosterone** is the main male reproductive hormone. It is made in the testes and stimulates sperm production.
The glands involved in human reproduction are the ovaries and the testes.
Oestrogen (ovary) is the main female hormone. Testosterone (testes) is the main male hormone.
Secondary sex characteristics, such as breast development, depend on these hormones.
From puberty, an egg is released about every 28 days.

sections.heading: The four hormones of the menstrual cycle

blocks.text: In the menstrual cycle, the lining of the uterus thickens and then breaks down. Four hormones control this. Tap each one to see where it is made and what it does.

diagram.alt: Tap a reproductive hormone to see where it is made and what it does.
diagram.prompt: Tap a hormone to learn its job, then test yourself.

parts.name: FSH
parts.detail: Follicle stimulating hormone. Made in the pituitary gland. It causes an egg to mature in a follicle in the ovary.

parts.name: LH
parts.detail: Luteinising hormone. Made in the pituitary gland. It stimulates the release of the egg (ovulation).

parts.name: Oestrogen
parts.detail: Made in the ovary. It causes the lining of the uterus to thicken.

parts.name: Progesterone
parts.detail: Made in the ovary, by the empty follicle (corpus luteum), after ovulation. It maintains the lining of the uterus.

parts.name: Testosterone
parts.detail: The main male hormone. Made in the testes. It stimulates sperm production.

items: FSH matures an egg. LH releases it.
Oestrogen thickens the uterus lining. Progesterone maintains it.
FSH and LH come from the pituitary gland. Oestrogen and progesterone come from the ovary.

blocks.text: The cycle lasts about 28 days. These stages show where each hormone acts.

items.text: FSH makes an egg mature in a follicle. The follicle makes oestrogen.
Oestrogen makes the lining of the uterus thicken.
LH stimulates the release of the egg, around the middle of the cycle.
The empty follicle (corpus luteum) makes progesterone, which maintains the lining.
The lining breaks down and is shed. This is the period.

blocks.text: How the four hormones affect each other is covered in the next note (AQA: Higher tier).

items: Each stage links a hormone to its job.
If there is no fertilised egg, the uterus lining breaks down.

checks.q: Name the hormone that stimulates the release of an egg, and the gland that makes it.
checks.a: LH (luteinising hormone), made in the pituitary gland.

checks.q: What is the job of progesterone in the menstrual cycle, and where is it made?
checks.a: It maintains the lining of the uterus. It is made in the ovary, by the corpus luteum (empty follicle).

checks.q: A woman makes no FSH. Explain why she may have underdeveloped breasts.
checks.a: Without FSH, follicles do not develop, so there is a lack of oestrogen. Breast development depends on oestrogen.

worked_example.question: A 27-year-old woman was infertile. A doctor tested a sample of the woman's blood. The test did not detect any follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) in the woman's blood. Before treatment with FSH, the woman had underdeveloped breasts. Explain why the lack of FSH in the woman's blood caused underdeveloped breasts.
answer_points: Lack of FSH causes a lack of oestrogen production, because follicles do not develop or mature (1).
Breast development, like other female secondary sexual characteristics, is dependent on oestrogen (1).
worked_example.tip: Link FSH to oestrogen first, then oestrogen to breast development.

worked_example.question: During clomifene therapy, the woman has a blood test on day 20 of the menstrual cycle. The blood test shows a high level of progesterone. Explain the cause of this high level of progesterone on day 20 of the menstrual cycle.
answer_points: Day 20 is after ovulation, after the egg has been released (1).
So the corpus luteum produces progesterone (1).
This is to maintain the lining of the uterus (1). Any two of these three points score.
worked_example.tip: Link the timing, the source and the job of the hormone.

worked_example.question: Different hormones control the human menstrual cycle. Complete the sentences to describe how the menstrual cycle is controlled. Use words from the list. Each word can be used once, more than once, or not at all. fetus, follicle, FSH, oestrogen, progesterone. The hormone released by the pituitary gland is called ____. This hormone acts on the ovary and causes the growth of a ____. The hormone that maintains the lining of the uterus is called ____.
answer_points: FSH is released by the pituitary gland (1).
It acts on the ovary and causes the growth of a follicle (1).
Progesterone maintains the lining of the uterus (1).
worked_example.tip: Match each hormone to its gland first, then to its job.

worked_example.question: Describe the role of oestrogen at puberty.
answer_points: Oestrogen causes the development of the secondary sexual characteristics.
worked_example.tip: Three of these points score. Name changes that oestrogen causes in the body.

items: **Oestrogen** (females): breasts grow, hips widen, pubic and body hair grows, and the menstrual cycle starts.
**Testosterone** (males): voice deepens, facial and body hair grows, muscles develop, and the testes and penis enlarge.

blocks.text: (Supplement) In the menstrual cycle, progesterone is made in the ovary. In pregnancy, the placenta also makes progesterone and oestrogen.
(Supplement) Progesterone stays high in pregnancy. It:

items: maintains the lining of the uterus
inhibits contractions of the uterus wall
prevents FSH and LH release, so no more follicles develop and there is no ovulation or menstruation

worked_example.question:
Hormones control the menstrual cycle.

Describe the roles of FSH and LH in the menstrual cycle.
answer_points: FSH stimulates the release of oestrogen.
LH causes ovulation (the release of the egg).
LH stimulates the release of progesterone (and the development of the corpus luteum).
worked_example.tip: Two marks for each hormone: one for its effect on the egg, one for the hormone it stimulates.

items: **Oestrogen** (females): breasts grow, hips widen, pubic and body hair grows, and the menstrual cycle starts.
**Testosterone** (males): voice deepens, facial and body hair grows, muscles develop, and the testes and penis enlarge.

blocks.text: In the menstrual cycle, FSH and LH act on the ovary:

items: FSH matures the follicle and stimulates it to release oestrogen.
LH causes ovulation and stimulates the corpus luteum to release progesterone.
